The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
Why, in plain words: A code change to the shop stopped updating each shopper's saved running total for the current month when a purchase was recorded, but the shop's statements and checks still read that saved total, so it fell further behind what shoppers had actually bought.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 7d 0h 0m 58s {duration}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): none so far {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken - recommends: roll io-shop back
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #554 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' monthly spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
Incident: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop
Date: Nov 04, 2026, 04:00 UTC, not back to normal by Nov 11, 2026, 04:00:58 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:32:53 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 04:00:15 UTC
Ended by: Argus: recommended to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 04:00:58 UTC - roll io-shop back

Summary
The service broke at Nov 04, 04:00 UTC and was not back to normal by Nov 11, 04:00:58 UTC, at least 7 days 58 seconds later. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by no more than those hours vary on their own, if at all. A code change to the shop stopped updating each shopper's saved running total for the current month when a purchase was recorded, but the shop's statements and checks still read that saved total, so it fell further behind what shoppers had actually bought. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #554, for a person to review and merge. It was written against main, which does not contain the revision that ran: merged, it changes what runs only once a deploy carries it. Argus recommends this and did not take it: roll io-shop back. Every purchase recorded through either write path on the running revision could keep leaving shoppers' stored monthly totals short, and the totals already written wrong stay wrong in the monthly statements and spend figures that read them until someone rewrites them.

Impact
at least 7d 0h 0m 58s - since onset, still not back to normal
not measured by the metrics - peak error rate
not counted by the metrics - requests failed
none so far - customer loss (estimated)
AL1: What the alert found: 240 of 240 shopper totals do not reconcile with the purchases behind them. The widest is short by 1,297.31, and the oldest affected purchase was recorded at 2026-11-04T04:00:00Z. Found by the spend-integrity check, which runs every 7 days, so the fault is up to that old.

Root cause and contributing factors
The change removed the line in record_purchase that added each in-month purchase's price to the account's stored total_this_month_cents, on the reasoning that the month could be derived from the purchase history, yet left the stored field in place. The monthly statement still reads that field as the month total and divides it by the number of purchases to get the mean, the spend summary divides it by the number of this month's purchases, and the reconciliation check compares it with the sum of this month's purchase prices. So every purchase recorded afterwards left the stored figure further behind the purchases.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' stored monthly spend totals no longer matched the purchases behind them: each affected total came out short of what the shopper had bought this month.
  Evidence:
    AL1
why 1 Purchases recorded on the running code were added to the account and to the lifetime total, but the stored this-month total was left where it was. The reconciliation check compares that stored figure with the sum of the in-month purchases, so it found the stored figure short.
  Evidence:
    S1 src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py at 26f1d7e
    U4 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:109, in reconcile_monthly_totals: compares it with _bought_this_month(account), where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
    U5 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_reconciliation.py:115, in _the_disagreement_in: subtracts with it: _bought_this_month(account) - account.total_this_month_cents, where _bought_this_month(account) returns sum(purchase.price_cents for purchase in account.purchases if purchase.in_current_month)
why 2 Revision 26f1d7e, deployed at 03:59:32 UTC, removed the update to total_this_month_cents from record_purchase. As of Nov 11, 04:00:52 UTC, all 3 replicas were running that revision.
  Evidence:
    P2 03:59:32 UTC deploy 26f1d7e by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
    D1 Deployment of revision 26f1d7e to io-shop, compared against 4c810f2 - the revision deployed before it.
    T10 Nov 11 04:00:52 Investigator Agent: Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run revision 26f1d7e, deployed at Nov 04 03:59:32
  Ruled out:
    The earlier deploy of revision 4c810f2 at Nov 03, 23:59:32 UTC: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at 04:00 UTC, which is after the later deploy at 03:59:32 UTC.
      AL1
      P1 Nov 03, 2026, 23:59:32 UTC deploy 4c810f2 by kuki: from the ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App repository's deploy/ directory
      P2
    A flag change by anyone but Argus: Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour 1 minute before Nov 04 04:01.
      T13
why 3 The change stopped keeping the month total on the reasoning that it could be derived from the history, but it left the stored field in place, and the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation check all still read that stored field.
  Evidence:
    D1
    S1
    U1 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:650, in the_mean_purchase_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought)
    U2 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:882, in _compared_with_usual: reads it: this_month_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
    U3 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/monthly_statement.py:918, in render_monthly_statement: reads it: month_total_cents = account.total_this_month_cents
    U4
    U5
    U6 total_this_month_cents at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, in average_spend_per_item_this_month: divides with it: account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month)
Contributing factors
- The only thing that found the drift was the spend-integrity check, which runs once every 7 days. No more frequent check was seen comparing stored monthly totals with the purchases behind them. (AI-4)
- Before the change was deployed, no check was seen that records purchases through the ledger's write paths and confirms the stored monthly total still matches the purchases. (AI-5)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | Revision 26f1d7e, deployed 03:59:32 UTC, changed record_purchase in purchase_ledger.py so it stopped maintaining total_this_month_cents. Account totals written from then on disagree with the purchases behind them. Serving stayed healthy, so no metric moved. The oldest wrong record is dated 04:00 UTC, right after the deploy. | 0.80 | never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken
C2 | The deployment 26f1d7e shipped faulty code that no longer maintains the monthly total. The alternative reading is that the deploy is simply a bad code release. | 0.15 | never tried: nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken

Trigger
Suspected, not confirmed: io-shop was deployed from 4c810f2 to 26f1d7e at 03:59:32 UTC, by kuki.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | Nov 11 04:00:58 | Refused to act on C1 - nothing would say whether the action that would test the candidate worked inside the time Argus waits, so it is recommended rather than taken | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken
 | Nov 11 04:03:36 | Proposed a fix: PR #554 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 04:00 UTC. SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile fired at Nov 11, 2026, 04:00:13 UTC, 7 days 13 seconds later - its rule fires as soon as its condition holds.

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #554 | open
AI-2 | Roll io-shop back | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Export the accounts and run Code-Fix's repair script against them (scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py), first as a dry run and then with --apply, and load the corrected accounts back. Do this once a revision that maintains the month total is running, and before the month rolls over. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Run the spend-integrity check that compares stored monthly totals with the purchases far more often than it runs now. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Add a test that runs for every change to the purchase ledger. It should record purchases through each write path (record_purchase, record_purchase_deriving_the_month and record_a_purchase both ways) and assert that reconcile_monthly_totals reports nothing for the result. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the on-call rotation so that a person is paged when it fires. | process | unassigned | - | open
Argus declined to act, and recommends: roll io-shop back

Lessons learned
What went well
- 38 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 26f1d7e changed.
- 40 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour 1 minute before Nov 04 04:01.
- 45 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus left for a person to do - rolling io-shop back for C1.
- 3 minutes 23 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #554.
What went wrong
- The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it, so the rollback Argus recommended waited on a person noticing it.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What each deployment looked into changed
D1 | Deployment of revision 26f1d7e to io-shop, compared against 4c810f2 - the revision deployed before it.
modified src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py
  @@ -28,26 +28,23 @@
   
   
   def record_purchase(account: Account, purchase: Purchase) -> Account:
  -    """The account with this purchase written into it, and both totals moved.
  +    """The account with this purchase written into it, and its total moved.
   
  -    How a purchase has always been recorded. Each total is added to rather than
  -    worked out again: the account already carries what has been spent, and a sale
  -    changes it by exactly the price of the thing sold.
  +    How a purchase is recorded. The lifetime total is added to rather than worked
  +    out again: the account already carries what has been spent, and a sale changes
  +    it by exactly the price of the thing sold.
   
  -    The month is the part worth reading twice. A purchase counts towards the
  -    month's total only if it falls in the month being counted, so that addition is
  -    conditional where the lifetime one is not - and a shopper backfilling an older
  -    order leaves this month's figure exactly where it was.
  +    The month is no longer carried. Every purchase says whether it falls in the
  +    current month, so what a shopper has spent this month adds up from the history
  +    whenever anybody wants it - exactly as the lifetime average is derived from the
  +    purchases rather than read off the account. A second copy of a figure the
  +    purchases already hold is a copy that has to be kept in step, and the cheapest
  +    way to keep it in step is not to keep it.
       """
       return replace(
           account,
           purchases=(*account.purchases, purchase),
  -        total_cents=account.total_cents + purchase.price_cents,
  -        total_this_month_cents=(
  -            account.total_this_month_cents + purchase.price_cents
  -            if purchase.in_current_month
  -            else account.total_this_month_cents
  -        )
  +        total_cents=account.total_cents + purchase.price_cents
       )
   
   
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | Which code each claim is about:
• The deployed revision 26f1d7e is not in main's history, so I have not read it. The claim that it removed the total_this_month_cents update from record_purchase comes from the investigation's deploy diff, not from code I saw.
• On main, in src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py, record_purchase still moves total_this_month_cents. But main has the same fault in record_purchase_deriving_the_month, which record_a_purchase calls when derive_the_month is true. That function adds the purchase and moves total_cents, but copies total_this_month_cents across unchanged. That is the same omission the investigation describes in the deployed revision. So turning that path on, or deploying the branch again, would leave stored month totals out of line with the purchases again.

The fix, in src/io_shop/purchase_ledger.py: record_purchase_deriving_the_month now sets total_this_month_cents to the sum of price_cents over the account's purchases (including the new one) where in_current_month is true. So the path writes the month total it derives instead of dropping it. An account with a total that has already drifted gets the correct figure the next time it is written through this path. record_purchase and record_a_purchase are unchanged, and the field keeps its name and type.

Tests (tests/io_shop/test_purchase_ledger.py): three new cases. They assert that the deriving path, called directly and through record_a_purchase(..., derive_the_month=True), leaves total_this_month_cents equal to the sum of this month's purchase prices. One case also asserts that reconcile_monthly_totals reports nothing for the result. Against main as it stands, they are written to fail, because the deriving path returns the account's old month total. Nothing has run them.

Repair (scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py): the patch only prevents new wrong totals. It does not fix the ones already written. This one-off script reads accounts as JSON lines. It passes them to reconcile_monthly_totals and takes the shopper ids that come back as disagreeing. For those accounts only, it sets total_this_month_cents to the sum of this month's purchase prices and leaves every other field of the input line as it was. It is a dry run unless --apply is passed, in which case it writes only the corrected accounts. Either way it prints how many accounts it checked and changed. The JSON-lines format is my assumption, since I don't know how the store exports or loads accounts: whoever runs it has to export the accounts in that shape and load the corrected ones back. The script has not been run. A person has to run it, ideally after this fix is deployed and before the month rolls over, because in_current_month is what it sums by.

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, the monthly spend totals shown to shoppers who made purchases this month came out lower than what they had actually bought. A code change to the shop stopped updating each shopper's saved running total for the month whenever a purchase was recorded. The shop's statements and checks still read that saved total, so it fell further behind with every purchase. The problem lasted {duration}. Argus estimates the cost to the shop in takings at {customer_loss}. Nobody was paged, so no one on call was pulled in to respond. Argus found a suspected cause but chose not to act on it, because nothing would show whether the test action had worked within the time Argus waits. Instead, Argus recommends rolling io-shop back. Argus also proposed a fix, PR #554, which is open as a draft and has not been run. Neither step has changed the shop yet.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.
